# True Effort Score

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.swift from the Quiver 1.6.0 public API. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every API below exists in Quiver 1.0.0 and later unless it is tagged *(since X)*. Each entry is the declaration, then the first line of its documentation.

## TrueEffortScore

`struct TrueEffortScore` — `TrueEffortScore` models a runner's effort using three components: a `Ridge` baseline to predict heart rate from workload, a `ResidualModel` to measure the gap, and a `Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors>` to classify effort. It tracks session history, scores runs in real time, and updates the baseline as new data is collected. *(since 1.6.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable.

- `var classifier: Pipeline<KNearestNeighbors> { get }` — The effort classifier, seeded from the population anchors and any personal labeled samples. Frozen after seeding, since re-fitting it on its own predictions would be self-training. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var baseline: TESBaseline? { get }` — The personal expected-heart-rate baseline, derived from `history`. nil at cold start; read its `equation()`, `coefficients`, and `conditioning` once present. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var history: [Workout] { get }` — The runner's accumulated workouts — the data the baseline is fit on, and the thing to persist. Grows as `finalize()` folds each run in; bounded by `historyWindow`, `minimumHistoryRuns`, and `historyLimit`. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let historyWindow: TimeInterval?` — How far back, in seconds, from the newest run the baseline learns. Runs that start earlier drop off, so the baseline keeps pace with a runner who is improving. nil keeps every run. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let minimumHistoryRuns: Int` — The fewest recent runs kept even when they fall outside `historyWindow`, so a runner returning from a break keeps a baseline. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let historyLimit: Int?` — The most workouts retained, oldest dropping off first, applied after the window and the floor. It bounds the refit cost for a runner who logs many runs. nil keeps all. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var sessionCount: Int { get }` — Sessions logged — the cold-start to established axis. The caller decides what "established" means; the model only reports the count. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let lambda: Double` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `let k: Int` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var location: WorkoutLocation` — Where the current run takes place, `.outdoor` unless set. Set it before the first sample: an indoor run records every grade as `indoorGrade` and is scored but not folded into history. Ending the run (`finalize()` or `discardRun()`) resets it to `.outdoor`. Changing it mid-run affects only later samples, and `finalize()` reads the value at the end. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `static let indoorGrade: Double` — The grade, in percent, recorded for every sample of an indoor run. The watch cannot sense treadmill incline, so an indoor run is scored as level ground at the usual 0.5% setting; an incline the runner sets on the belt is not reflected. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `init(lambda: Double = 0.01, k: Int = 3, historyWindow: TimeInterval? = 28 * 86_400, minimumHistoryRuns: Int = 8, historyLimit: Int? = 60)` — A brand-new runner: empty history, no personal baseline yet. The classifier is anchor- seeded from the population set, so a score exists from the first tick; `baseline == nil` is the cold-start tell. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `init(history: [Workout], labeledSamples: [[Double]] = [], labels: [EffortClass] = [], lambda: Double = 0.01, k: Int = 3, historyWindow: TimeInterval? = 28 * 86_400, minimumHistoryRuns: Int = 8, historyLimit: Int? = 60) throws` — Seeds from existing workouts and optional personal labeled samples, then fits the baseline once. Each labeled sample is a classifier feature row `[heartRate, pace, cadence, grade, verticalOscillation]`, appended to the bundled anchors, so the classifier never trains on less than the anchor set. Throws: `TESError.insufficientLabeledSamples` when k exceeds the labeled example count; `TESError.baselineDiverged` if the seed fit diverges. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `mutating func record(heartRate: Double, pace: Double, cadence: Double, grade: Double, verticalOscillation: Double, altitude: Double, at time: Date, hrTrust: Double = 1.0)` — Records one moment from its raw signals, stamped with an absolute time. The delta is derived internally, so the caller never tracks it. A non-positive delta is dropped, which self- discards a duplicate or out-of-order callback. The first sample of a run carries zero load but stamps the start; a post-resume gap advances wall clock only, never timer time or the run's start. `hrTrust` is the optical-sensor reliability, clamped to `0...1`; a fully doubted reading classifies on the kinematic signals alone. Grade is signed, negative for downhill; on an indoor run it is recorded as `indoorGrade` whatever the caller supplies. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `mutating func pause()` — Pauses the run. The paused span counts toward wall-clock `elapsedTime` but not `timerTime`. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `mutating func resume()` — Resumes the run. The next recorded sample re-seeds the clock across the paused gap. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `mutating func discardRun()` — Discards the in-progress run without folding it into history. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var currentScore: Double { get }` — The live True Effort Score, climbing through the run against the fixed 2700 anchor. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var currentEffort: EffortClass? { get }` — The classifier's effort band for the latest recorded sample, nil before the first sample. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var currentResidual: Double? { get }` — Observed minus expected heart rate for the latest sample, nil before a baseline exists. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var currentSignals: EffortSignals? { get }` — The latest sample's signals as z-scores against the classifier's training distribution, so a UI can spot which signal is an outlier — a large negative `grade` with a near-zero `heartRate` is the downhill signature. nil before the first sample. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var sampleCount: Int { get }` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var elapsedTime: TimeInterval { get }` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var timerTime: TimeInterval { get }` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `var isPaused: Bool { get }` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `mutating func finalize() -> TESResult?` — Closes the run: returns the breakdown, folds the run into history, and re-fits the baseline from the accumulated history (the classifier stays frozen). An indoor run returns its breakdown but leaves history and the baseline untouched. Returns nil when active `timerTime` is below the floor, in which case the run is cleared and not kept. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `static let anchorSamples: [[Double]]` — Classifier feature rows for the anchor set: [heartRate, pace, cadence, grade, vertOsc]. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `static let anchorLabels: [EffortClass]` — The effort labels parallel to `anchorSamples`. The old-hard rows split between `.threshold` (sustained race pace) and `.hard` (climb, descent, and above-threshold surges) by their kinematics; that split is a judgment call, provisional until the validation study. *(since 1.6.0)*

## TESError

`enum TESError` — What the seeding initializer can surface, as one catchable type, so a watch app can handle a failed seed without trapping. The empty init and the live loop do not throw, and decoding a saved model restores its baseline as stored without refitting, so a `TESError` comes only from seeding with existing runs. `.baselineDiverged` nests the underlying `GradientDescentError` whole, preserving its typed payload and description. *(since 1.6.0)*

Conforms to: Equatable, Error.

- `case insufficientLabeledSamples(k: Int, available: Int)` — The seeding init was asked for more neighbors than it has labeled examples. The empty init preconditions `k <= anchorSamples.count` instead. *(since 1.6.0)*
- `case baselineDiverged(GradientDescentError)` — The Ridge baseline diverged while fitting, preserved whole. *(since 1.6.0)*

## WorkoutLocation

`enum WorkoutLocation` — Where a run takes place. The watch cannot sense treadmill incline: its barometric altimeter measures a change in altitude, and a runner on an inclined belt never rises. An indoor run is therefore scored at a fixed level-ground grade and kept out of the personal baseline, so a grade the model cannot trust never shapes the runner's outdoor expectations. *(since 1.6.0)*

Conforms to: Codable, Equatable, Hashable.

- `init?(rawValue: String)` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `case outdoor` *(since 1.6.0)*
- `case indoor` *(since 1.6.0)*
